text: When one of you has a grievance against another, how dare you take it to court before the unrighteous instead of before the saints?
Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is to be judged by you, are you incompetent to try trivial cases?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the affairs of this life!
So if you have cases about everyday matters, why do you seat as judges those who count for nothing in the church?
I say this to shame you. Is there really no one among you wise enough to settle a dispute between brothers?
Instead, brother goes to court against brother—and that before unbelievers!
The very fact that you have lawsuits among yourselves is already a defeat for you. Why not rather accept the wrong? Why not rather let yourselves be cheated?
But instead you yourselves do wrong and cheat—and you do it to your own brothers.

Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral nor idolaters nor adulterers nor men who submit to homosexual acts nor those who practice them,
nor thieves nor the greedy nor drunkards nor revilers nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.

versions.text: nor thieves nor the greedy nor drunkards nor slanderers nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
versions.explanation: λοίδοροι refers to verbal abusers/revilers (those who insult others to their face), not slanderers (who speak falsely behind another's back, καταλάλοι). "Revilers" or "the verbally abusive" is more accurate and keeps the rhythm of the list.

text: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.

versions.text: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
versions.explanation: The base Greek text reads "the Lord Jesus" (Ἰησοῦ); "Christ" is an addition reflecting a variant reading. If retained, it should be noted in a footnote rather than placed in the text.

text: "Everything is permitted for me"—but not everything is beneficial. "Everything is permitted for me"—but I will not be mastered by anything.
"Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food"—and God will do away with both. But the body is not meant for sexual immorality; it is meant for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
And God, who raised the Lord, will also raise us by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? Never!
Or do you not know that anyone who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her? For it is said, "The two will become one flesh."
But whoever is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.
Flee sexual immorality. Every sin a person commits is outside the body, but the one who is sexually immoral sins against his own body.

versions.text: Flee sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the one who is sexually immoral sins against his own body.
versions.explanation: The word "other" is an interpretive addition not present in the Greek. While it smooths the logic, the plain reading "Every sin a person commits is outside the body" preserves Paul's rhetorical force; the clarification could be placed in a footnote instead.

text: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,

versions.text: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you received from God? You are not your own,
versions.explanation: The Greek uses the present tense ἔχετε ("you have"), stressing ongoing possession, rather than the past act of receiving.

text: for you were bought at a price. So glorify God with your body.
